newsitem.title: UK: Bulgaria down among otherwise healthy Bradys.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria down among otherwise healthy Bradys.

text.p: Bulgarian Bradys took a fresh knock on Monday on the disarray in the country's politics but the rest of the emerging debt market looked solid, traders said.

Bulgaria's ruling Socialists were in confusion after the resignation of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov but some traders doubted it would be enough to stop the country meeting debt repayments later this month.
"The market believes they will pay. It's (the payment issue) all people who don't know Bulgaria think about," one U.S. bank trader said.
One positive aspect is that the central bank has not been using up its reserves to defend the plunging lev.
The trader said there was some buying of Bradys at the lower levels.
Bulgarian IABs BGFLTH11=RR were down 5/8 of a point by mid-morning at 49-5/8 cents in the dollar, down about two percent since the end of last year.
"Bulgaria should continue into 1997 as the most volatile and risky of the Bradys, as well as the most lucrative, but naturally, the hardest to call," Indosuez Capital said.
"For those attracted by the scenario, we would look to buy on weakness for short-term holding through to the announcement of the currency board and the IMF facility," it added.
A new Bulgarian government, one of whose first tasks will be to negotiate a deal with the International Monetary Fund, is expected to be named by the end of this week.
Elsewhere, the market was looking fairly robust though Russia was largely ignored ahead of Tuesday's holiday there.
Latin Amercian debt is coming back into favour, with Mexico buoyed by an impending global bond issue which is expected to tighten spreads.
Some traders are tipping Brazil on the basis that its political outlook is positive. But others are more wary, pointing OUT the country's continuing trade deficit.
